cwe_name: Out-of-bounds read: data is read from past the end of a buffer

vulnerable.rationale: The shape function reads dimension 1 of input(0) without validating that the input rank is at least 2, so a hostile shape with rank < 2 can cause an out-of-bounds read in the shape metadata.

patched.rationale: The only externally influenced value, c->input(0), is guarded by WithRank(...,2) before c->Dim(input(0),1) reads dimension index 1, so the index is always in range; the remaining calls only build shape handles with no memory or size arithmetic that can be corrupted.

cwe_name: Null pointer dereference: a missing pointer is used as if it were there

vulnerable.rationale: The node name taken from attacker-controlled graph data (node.input(0)) is passed to graph.GetNode(), which yields nullptr for an unknown/empty name; the result is dereferenced in IsSwitch(*input_node) with no NULL check anywhere on the path, giving a crash/DoS.

patched.rationale: The only externally influenced data (node.input(0), parsed into a TensorId) is guarded: input_size() is checked before indexing, and the pointer returned by graph.GetNode is tested for nullptr before being dereferenced. No copy, size arithmetic or pointer lifetime hazard exists in this function.

cwe_name: Out-of-bounds write: data is written past the end of a buffer

lines.text: yank_copy_line(struct block_def *bd, long y_idx, int exclude_trailing_space)

vulnerable.rationale: With exclude_trailing_space, endspaces is zeroed, so s = textlen; for an empty line s == 0 and the while condition dereferences bd->textstart + s - 1 (i.e. textstart[-1]) before the s > 0 test, an out-of-bounds read; s can also go negative via mb_head_off, reading further before the buffer.

lines.text: yank_copy_line(struct block_def *bd, long y_idx, int exclude_trailing_space)

patched.rationale: The trailing-space scan is bounded by s > 0 and by mb_head_off, which never exceeds the offset from textstart, so pnew-- can never pass the start of the alloc'd buffer; the allocation covers startspaces+endspaces+textlen+1 and the NUL lands inside it. No reachable out-of-bounds write or read in this function.

cwe_name: Information exposure: data reaches someone who shouldn't see it

lines.text: int digest_generic_verify(struct digest *d, const unsigned char *md)

vulnerable.rationale: The expected digest/MAC (md) is compared with memcmp, which returns as soon as a differing byte is found, so verification time depends on how many leading bytes match. An attacker able to measure that timing can recover the secret digest byte by byte; a constant-time comparison is missing.

lines.text: int digest_generic_verify(struct digest *d, const unsigned char *md)

patched.rationale: The buffer is sized from digest_length(d) and both the digest_final write and the crypto_memneq compare use that same len, so no overflow; the compare is constant-time, all paths set ret, and tmp is freed exactly once. Remaining concerns (NULL md, zero digest_size) depend on caller/algorithm state outside this function.

vulnerable.rationale: bi->pixelsize is taken verbatim from the file at pos+18 (dbuf_getu16be returns 0 for a zero field) and is used as the divisor in (bi->rowbytes*8)/bi->pixelsize with no zero check on any path, so a crafted PixMap with bits/pixel=0 causes an integer division by zero and crashes the parser.

patched.rationale: All field reads go through the bounds-checked dbuf accessors, and the only arithmetic hazard, the division by bi->pixelsize, is guarded by pixelsize>0 (the value comes from a u16 read, so it cannot be negative). No unchecked copy, size computation or dereference exists in this function.

patched.rationale: All writes into the caller-supplied `cap` are size-bounded: `labellen` is the minimum of the destination and source array sizes, `bus_info`/`driver` use sizeof, and `reserved` is zeroed. cwe_name: Null pointer dereference: a missing pointer is used as if it were there

vulnerable.rationale: hmhd is taken from trak->Media->information->InfoHeader and dereferenced at line 4 (hmhd->type) before the NULL test at line 7, which itself shows a NULL InfoHeader is expected. A NULL value therefore causes a null-pointer dereference before any guard runs.

patched.rationale: Line 3 walks trak->Media->information->InfoHeader with no NULL test on trak, Media or information; a file whose trak box lacks a mdia/info child (or a NULL trak argument) makes this chained dereference fault before any of the later hmhd guards run.

cwe_name: Out-of-bounds write: data is written past the end of a buffer

lines.text: static size_t send_control_msg(VirtIOSerial *vser, void *buf, size_t len)

vulnerable.rationale: The caller-controlled length `len` is copied into the guest-supplied buffer elem.in_sg[0].iov_base with no comparison against elem.in_sg[0].iov_len (the descriptor's actual size), so an oversized len writes past the end of the mapped buffer, causing a heap/out-of-bounds write.

lines.text: static size_t send_control_msg(VirtIOSerial *vser, void *buf, size_t len)
/* TODO: detect a buffer that's too short, set NEEDS_RESET */

patched.rationale: The guest-controlled destination scatter/gather total (elem.in_num/in_sg) is never compared against len before iov_from_buf, and virtqueue_push unconditionally reports len bytes written, so a short guest buffer yields an unchecked/short write with the full length claimed (the TODO admits the missing check).

cwe_name: Integer overflow: a number grows past what its type can hold

vulnerable.rationale: The only untrusted value, `size`, is funnelled through TfLiteIntArrayGetSizeInBytes and gated by `alloc_size <= 0`, which rejects negative/overflowed-to-nonpositive results, and malloc's return is checked before `ret->size` is written. No unchecked copy, arithmetic or dereference is visible in this function; any truncation would live in the unseen helper.

patched.rationale: Untrusted int `size` feeds the allocation-size computation; the only guard, `alloc_size <= 0`, compares an unsigned size_t, so it can never catch a wrapped/truncated value. A hostile size then yields a small malloc while ret->size records the large requested count, giving a heap buffer overflow on later data[] access.

cwe_name: Out-of-bounds write: data is written past the end of a buffer

lines.text: mrb_name_error(mrb, mid, "method '%n' not defined in %C", mid, c);

vulnerable.rationale: The method table pointer `h` is NULL-tested before `mt_del`, the format string passed to mrb_name_error is a compile-time literal (no format-string injection), and no size arithmetic, copy or unchecked dereference of attacker-controlled data occurs. Remaining concerns (NULL class, iclass state) are external program-state assumptions, not visible defects.

lines.text: mrb_name_error(mrb, mid, "method '%n' not defined in %C", mid, c);

patched.rationale: The method table pointer h is checked before mt_del, and every failure path ends in mrb_name_error raising an exception; there are no copies, size arithmetic, allocations or format-string inputs, and the only remaining concern (c being NULL) is an assumption about caller state, not a visible defect.

cwe_name: Improper Check or Handling of Exceptional Conditions

vulnerable.rationale: The only externally controlled value, the int index widened to size_t, is passed to buf->Peek(), which reports out-of-range via status and is gated by OP_REQUIRES_OK; the output loop is bounded by tuple.size() matched against num_outputs(). No unchecked sink is visible.

patched.rationale: The only externally influenced loop bound, tuple.size(), is explicitly required to equal ctx->num_outputs() before the set_output loop, so no out-of-range index is reachable; buf is used only after OP_REQUIRES_OK succeeds, and no unchecked arithmetic or copy exists.
